 Nagaland Lottery Publishes October 17 Draw Schedule and Prize Details 
 Nagaland Lottery Publishes October 17 Draw Schedule and Prize Details
 Emily Johnson

 Nagaland's state-run lottery program scheduled three draws for Saturday, October 17, 2026, with Dear Vision at 1 p.m., Dear Elite at 6 p.m., and Dear Lucky at 8 p.m. According to results coverage published by Goodreturns, each draw offered a first prize of ₹1 crore, while ticket holders must verify winning numbers against official records before claiming awards.
 The published prize structure includes six categories: a first prize of ₹1 crore, a consolation prize of ₹1,000, a second prize of ₹10,000, a third prize of ₹500, a fourth prize of ₹250, and a fifth prize of ₹120. Goodreturns identified the three Saturday draws by their respective names and scheduled times.

 However, the supplied October 17 coverage does not provide a complete set of verified winning numbers for all three draws. Ticket holders therefore should distinguish the announced schedule and prize structure from confirmed individual results.

 Eastern Mirror's October 17 reporting also documented results for two Friday draws held on October 16. The Dear Victory Friday draw at 1 p.m. recorded winning ticket number 70B 30467 for the first prize of ₹1 crore, according to information attributed to Nagaland State Lotteries.
 The Dear Crown Friday draw, held at 6 p.m. on October 16, recorded ticket number 93A 43317 as the first-prize winner. Eastern Mirror reported that the winning ticket was eligible for ₹1 crore and that the ticket price was ₹7 for each of these two draws.
 Separately, Eastern Mirror reported that the Dear Star Thursday draw on October 15 produced first-prize ticket number 95E 75331. The publication identified the draw as the 50th edition and listed a first prize of ₹1 crore, with tickets priced at ₹7.
 Also Read 
 Turkey Forecasts Showers in 10 Provinces on October 20 
 These reported results concern separate draws on different dates and should not be confused with the October 17 Saturday results. Official result documents remain the reference for confirming a ticket's number, series, and eligibility.
 According to Sentinel Assam, Nagaland's lottery program originated in 1972 under the supervision of the Finance Department as a source of state revenue. The same report states that lotteries have been legally permitted in Nagaland since 1967 and identifies the state among 13 Indian states that allow lottery operations.
 The report describes a standard schedule of draws at 1 p.m., 6 p.m., and 8 p.m. It also lists ticket series and serial-number ranges that vary by draw, with serial numbers running from 00000 to 99999 and ticket prices generally stated as ₹6 in its schedule.

 For prize claims, Sentinel Assam says winners must submit the original winning ticket, a completed claim form, government-recognized photo identification, and passport-sized photographs. Tickets must remain intact, and tampered or mutilated tickets will not be accepted.
 The publication further states that prizes up to ₹10,000 may be paid through distributors, stockists, agents, or sellers authorized by the state government. Winners should follow the applicable official claim requirements for their prize category.
 Results are published through official government lottery records and other reporting platforms, including Eastern Mirror. Director Zhothisa Dawhuo also identified lottery-related YouTube channels as additional places where results can be viewed, according to Eastern Mirror's reporting.
